issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron is at the checkout!
issues.justification: The joke is a blend of 'strike while the iron is hot' and 'don't leave the cash desk' (a Soviet-era idiom). 'At the checkout' is a literal rendering that does not work as a comic malapropism in English, and it also weakens the recurring catchphrase used by the Boss.

issues.source_quote: Они же уверены, что Вы ничего не знаете, Они попытаются получить свой товар бесплатно
issues.translation_quote: Mikhail Ivanovich, could someone else wear this cast instead of me?
issues.justification: Not an error in itself, but the earlier line 'Ясно, Нью-Йорк' / 'A cast!' is fine. The real issue: 'Закрытый перелом' vs 'открытый перелом' joke. Translated as 'simple fracture' vs 'open fracture', which loses the closed/open contrast ('closed' is the standard term) and weakens the pun about hidden contents.

issues.source_quote: Обои!... Убью!
issues.translation_quote: Both of you! I'll kill you!
issues.justification: Oversimplified; also the line 'Руки... уверх!' is fine, but the earlier comic line 'Как говорил один мой знакомый, покойник: Я слишком много знал...' is fine. The key issue is 'Zhorzh'-style malapropism loss: Lyolik's mispronounced speech ('Усё', 'сымем', 'усе') is entirely normalized, losing his comic voice.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках! Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: Drop dead! I hope I see you in your coffin, in white slippers! I hope you live on nothing but your salary!
issues.justification: The neighbour's Odessa/Yiddish-flavoured vernacular ('у гробу', 'у белых тапках') is lost; the English is standard and flat, losing the characteristic voice and humor.

issues.source_quote: Вы в самодеятельности участвуете? Участвую. Зачем я соврал, я ж не учавствую?
issues.translation_quote: Do you take part in amateur dramatics? I do. Why did I lie? I don't!
issues.justification: 'Самодеятельность' refers to amateur talent/art groups in Soviet culture; 'amateur dramatics' is narrower. Acceptable but loses the Soviet cultural flavour.

issues.source_quote: Поскользнулся... - Упал. - Упал. Закрытый перелом...
issues.translation_quote: A simple fracture
issues.justification: 'Simple fracture' is a recurring mistranslation of 'закрытый перелом' (closed fracture). It is used consistently throughout, and it destroys the closed/open wordplay in Nadya's line ('не закрытый, а открытый перелом').

issues.source_quote: В измене!
issues.translation_quote: Treason!
issues.justification: Here 'измена' means marital infidelity/betrayal and Senya responds 'мать моих детей'. In the Russian the confusion is between infidelity and treason; 'Treason' mistranslates the line and removes the ambiguity that fuels the joke.

issues.source_quote: Нет, мне надо посоветоваться с шефом! С начальством...
issues.translation_quote: No, I must consult the Boss! My superior...
issues.justification: Lyolik, in the taxi, is posing as police. The line is a garbled slip betraying that he has a 'boss'; the translation is acceptable but the earlier slip 'Козадоев' / 'Казладоев' name-mangling jokes are only partly carried.

issues.source_quote: Облико морале… ферштейн?
issues.translation_quote: Moral standards... verstehen?
issues.justification: 'Облико морале' is a pseudo-Latin/Italian mock phrase; the rendering loses the comic faux-foreign flavor of the original. Also the Russian is 'ферштейн' and the English rendered 'verstehen' changes the form.

issues.source_quote: Эти игрушки идиотские!
issues.translation_quote: Those idiotic toys!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but 'Тлетворное влияние Запада' is rendered neutrally; the bureaucratic Soviet cliché tone is somewhat flattened.

issues.source_quote: Простите, погорячился...
issues.translation_quote: Sorry, I lost my temper...
issues.justification: Acceptable, but earlier 'Что она мне хочет сказать, что что-то случилось' etc. fine. The key error: 'Дальше следует непереводимая игра слов' is rendered OK. However, 'Он точно с теплохода' is rendered 'the Mikhail Svetlov' without 'ship' context, minor.

issues.source_quote: Читали в «Неделе», отдел для, дома для семьи...
issues.translation_quote: Did you read the home and family section in The Week?
issues.justification: 'Неделя' was a Soviet weekly newspaper supplement (Izvestia); 'The Week' loses this cultural reference but is retained consistently. Minor.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: That's "c'est la vie," as they say here...
issues.justification: 'У них' means 'over there/abroad' (the West); 'here' is wrong, since the speaker is back home or speaking of foreigners. Also the deliberate grammatical gender slip 'такова сё ля ви' is lost.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш любимый шеф, если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: As our beloved Boss says, if someone's an idiot, it's for life.
issues.justification: Acceptable; the 'Boss' catchphrase pattern is preserved. Minor naturalness only.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a great big stack of tickets and you'll win... A waterworks!
issues.justification: The rhyme (пачку/водокачку) that makes the lottery slogan comic is lost; the English has no rhyme and the joke of an absurd prize in a pat slogan does not land.

issues.source_quote: на полагающуюся мне по закону премию
issues.translation_quote: With the reward I'm entitled to by law
issues.justification: Fine. But 'Мы вообще дальше Дубровки никуда не ездили' fine. Instead: 'Наши люди в булочную на такси не ездят!' is rendered 'Our sort of people', which loses the Soviet 'наши люди' sense (ordinary Soviet citizens).

issues.source_quote: Фрис-стрит, рыбна улица, - Аптека «Чиканук»...
issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, Fish Street, - The Chikanuk pharmacy...
issues.justification: The original 'рыбна улица' is a deliberate mangling of the foreign-sounding phrase; the English 'Fish Street' normalizes it and loses the comic mispronunciation.

issues.source_quote: Пейте. Пейте, пейте...
issues.translation_quote: Drink. Go on, drink...
issues.justification: Fine. Minor: 'Simple fracture' repetition is more problematic.

issues.source_quote: Ха-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га!
issues.translation_quote: Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!
issues.justification: The Boss's distinctive villain laugh 'Ха-га-га' is normalized into generic 'ha-ha', losing a recurring character signature.

issues.source_quote: Скажите, пожалуйста, Вы давно знаете гражданина Горбункова С. С.? ... Ясно - собутыльник!
issues.translation_quote: Ten years, unfortunately!
issues.justification: Acceptable. However, 'Козлодоев' comic name mangling ('Kozlodoyev... Kozodoyev! Kozladoyev!') is mostly retained but 'козёл' connotation is lost.

issues.source_quote: Свободно? Занято!
issues.translation_quote: Is this seat free? Taken!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Мя-аув!
issues.translation_quote: Meow!
issues.justification: Acceptable.
